summary: The native Android Home screen's machine list uses the Connections screen's row: status dot, name, short fingerprint, then a lock and Encrypted, Not encrypted, local only, or Cloud IAP, and the address. A refused ws:// row shows the amber hint with Scan new QR and Use Cloud IAP. A tap on a certificate-changed row opens the certificate sheet (Scan QR again, Remove machine, Not now) instead of the machine. Home now applies the release rule that refuses plain ws:// to another computer, as the Connections screen already did.

desktop.reason: The desktop has no phone Home screen. Its Devices & machines tab is unchanged.

reactNativeIos.reason: The iOS Home (ConnectionsScreen.tsx, Recents then machines, see ios-home-recents) draws its machine list with the shared MachineRow, the same row as before, so there is no second Home row to align.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No wire, API or shared copy change. The rows read the existing copy in ConnectionSecurity.kt, already checked against tests/fixtures/connection-security-copy.json.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing new is stored. Row states come from the saved address and in-memory connection state, as on the Connections screen.

automated: Robolectric HomeMachineRowsTest renders HomeScreen: pinned, local and IAP rows show their transport copy and the short fingerprint; a refused row shows the amber hint and its two buttons call rescan and Cloud IAP; a certificate-changed row opens the sheet, not the machine, and Remove machine then Remove calls remove.
notExercised: Not run on a phone or an emulator. No screenshot test covers Home: the store screenshots open Connections from Home with no machines.
